principles: Local CLI admissibility is the core proof boundary; server production receipt completion is external adapter scope.
Preserve fail-closed evidence semantics while removing productionDone eligibility from local defaults.
Avoid broad Authority deletion; demote the core claim path first.
drivers: User wants to delete or demote Authority Server production receipt as a core dependency
Current registry still lets authority-receipt-ref be productionDoneEligible
The local admissibility contract now has version support and scanner coverage after B-fbfb

options.name: A: Demote local productionDone eligibility only
pros: Keeps historical/external Authority adapter code readable
Directly removes local core dependency on production receipt completion
cons: Authority-related names remain in adapters/docs as external or legacy scope

options.name: B: Delete all Authority client and receipt code
pros: Strongest simplification if server path is truly abandoned
cons: Large blast radius across tests, docs, baselines, handoff, usage ledger, and authority client flows

options.name: C: Documentation-only demotion
cons: Leaves productionDoneEligible=true in code, so the core route still exists

chosen: A: Demote local productionDone eligibility only
rationale: Option A matches the user intent without turning this into a repository-wide Authority deletion. The core problem is that local proof-admissibility still models authority-receipt-ref as productionDone eligible; changing that and updating tests/docs removes the core dependency while preserving external compatibility.

preMortem.scenario: Local DONE gates accidentally start requiring server receipt again
preMortem.trigger: A test or registry path still treats authority-receipt-ref as productionDoneEligible
preMortem.consequence: The CLI-first proof model remains confusing and brittle
preMortem.mitigation: Assert authority-receipt-ref production-completion returns productionDoneEligible=false in proof-admissibility smoke

preMortem.scenario: Broad Authority deletion breaks unrelated command surfaces
preMortem.trigger: Implementation removes authority client modules instead of demoting the core claim path
preMortem.consequence: Large unrelated regressions and blocked validation
preMortem.mitigation: Restrict allowed paths to proof-admissibility core/tests and the hardening doc

preMortem.scenario: Docs overclaim that Authority support is gone everywhere
preMortem.trigger: Hardening plan wording says deleted instead of external/legacy adapter scope
preMortem.consequence: Future hosts misunderstand remaining Authority client code
preMortem.mitigation: Use precise wording: external adapter/future work, not local core route
